reason: The supplied measurements show large timing variation and no repeatable promoted gain, so they do not support a performance claim for any proposal. I rank narrow assembly edits with lower correctness and timed-call risks first. Tile scheduling, vector access, and scratch lifetime keep the four ZA accumulators and avoid new packing. Macroblock and loop-order changes carry more traversal risk. Packing proposals rank last because they alter both data layout and compute traversal and add timed allocation and copy work. The tail overflow check is a safety change, not a throughput experiment.
